notes: The competing reading of a kid would mark עִזִּים unrepresented, but rule 30 forbids leaving a morpheme whose sense the one English word carries outside the unit.
לְפָנֶיךָ divides as rule 30 directs: the preposition and construct noun fuse into the single for, headed on the construct (rule 23), while the suffix keeps its own thee under rule 18.
make ready heads on make, since עָשָׂה's own lexeme is the making; rule 44's light-verb clause moves the head only where the supplied complement carries the lexeme.
